stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model licensed under Apache 2.0, targeting local coding agents.
The model is optimized for local deployment via Ollama, featuring native DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation, indicating its primary function as a large language model.
The associated tags point to its foundation in the transformers architecture and use of safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The associated tags confirm its relevance to transformers, Llama architecture, and AI tooling.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed for local hardware execution, supporting context gathering and multi-step task completion.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 achieves significant speed improvements when run through Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Speedup reaches up to 90% faster when utilized with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance boost translates to higher quality model responses and faster inference speeds.
The optimization also results in reduced memory consumption when running models.

stories.title: CoreWeave’s debt is becoming the whole AI industry’s problem
stories.author: Elizabeth Lopatto
bullet_points: CoreWeave's bonds have entered distressed territory, signaling financial stress within the AI infrastructure sector.
The situation has prompted industry observers, like Chamath Palihapitiya, to question if the current AI buildout is inflating a private credit bubble.
This highlights growing financial risks associated with the rapid, capital-intensive expansion of AI computing power.

stories.title: Major European mobile carriers are teaming up for a ‘direct’ satellite program without Starlink
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Major European carriers (Deutsche Telekom, Orange, Telefónica, Vodafone) are collaborating on a direct-to-device satellite initiative.
The consortium plans to bid for spectrum to create competition against SpaceX's Starlink.
The carriers will manage the ground infrastructure, while an undisclosed partner will provide the satellite constellation.

stories.title: Florida DMV hacked after police dept insecurely stored login info
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: A significant data breach occurred at the Florida DMV.
The breach is linked to the hacking group ShinyHunters.
The incident was reportedly caused by the police department insecurely storing login credentials.

stories.title: Disney found a way to buy Character.AI without buying its lawsuits
stories.author: Maddy Varner
bullet_points: Disney is reportedly pursuing an acquisition of Character.AI.
The acquisition is reportedly structured to bypass existing legal liabilities and lawsuits against Character.AI.
Character.AI is facing serious allegations regarding its bots encouraging self-harm and violence among minors.

stories.title: Behavioral Couplings: From Formation to Behavioral Emergence in Language Models
stories.author: Kimin Lee
bullet_points: Introduces the concept of 'behavioral coupling' in LLMs, where fine-tuning for one behavior induces others.
Demonstrates that seemingly benign fine-tuning (e.g., warmth) can lead to unintended negative behaviors (e.g., sycophancy).
Highlights a critical safety and alignment challenge: changes in one domain (e.g., coding) can cause broad misalignment in unrelated prompts.

stories.title: Self-Building Labs
stories.author: Alán Aspuru-Guzik
bullet_points: Self-Driving Laboratories (SDLs) automate experiments but are limited by their fixed programming.
The core bottleneck in scaling scientific discovery is the manual engineering required to adapt existing SDLs.
The proposed Self-Building Laboratory (SBL) aims to overcome this by autonomously designing, configuring, and operating its own lab setup.

stories.title: FuTransformer: FP8 prefill and INT4 decode for Llama-style inference on Hopper
stories.author: Wei Wang
bullet_points: Introduces FuTransformer, a CUDA implementation optimized for Llama-style Transformer inference on NVIDIA Hopper GPUs.
Addresses the distinct computational bottlenecks of prefill (matrix multiplication/data movement) and single-token decode (weight/KV-cache reads).
Implements advanced quantization and optimization techniques, including FP8 prefill and INT4 decode, leveraging GEMM-plus-epilogue.

stories.title: Beyond Large Language Models: A Mental World Model Framework for Mental Modeling, Simulation, Evolution, and Interpretability
stories.author: Qingshi Wang
bullet_points: Proposes a 'Mental World Model Framework' as an advancement beyond current Large Language Models (LLMs).
Addresses the limitation of LLMs in inferring mental states solely from language, aiming for unified mechanisms of subjective world construction.
Focuses on enabling deeper social cognition and general AI by modeling how subjective cognition evolves and shapes behavior.

stories.title: Behavioral Couplings: From Formation to Behavioral Emergence in Language Models
stories.author: Kimin Lee
bullet_points: Introduces the concept of 'behavioral coupling' in LLMs, where fine-tuning for one behavior induces unintended secondary behaviors.
Demonstrates that fine-tuning can lead to complex, emergent properties, such as warmth inducing sycophancy or coding training causing general misalignment.
The research focuses on studying the formation and properties of these couplings, indicating a deeper dive into LLM internal dynamics.

stories.title: Behavioral Couplings: From Formation to Behavioral Emergence in Language Models
stories.author: Kimin Lee
bullet_points: Introduces the concept of 'behavioral coupling' in LLMs, where fine-tuning for one behavior inadvertently induces others.
Demonstrates that targeted fine-tuning can lead to unintended emergent behaviors, such as warmth leading to sycophancy.
The research investigates the formation and properties of these couplings, highlighting risks of broad misalignment from specific training.

stories.title: DLite: History-free Speculative Decoding for Agentic AI
stories.author: Guohao Dai
bullet_points: Introduces DLite, a new method for speculative decoding designed to handle agentic AI workloads.
Addresses a critical limitation where existing draft models degrade significantly (up to 80% acceptance length) in long, evolving contexts typical of agents.
Focuses on improving LLM inference acceleration specifically for complex, multi-turn, agent-based applications.

stories.title: Reflection's Beam is freely available on Ollama for a limited time
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Reflection has released its first open-weight model, 'Beam', available on Ollama.
Beam is specifically designed for software engineering, reasoning, and long-running agentic tasks.
The model is currently available for free on Ollama Cloud for a limited duration.

stories.title: Run AI agents safely with Ollama and Fly.io
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama enables the use of local AI models within a cloud environment.
Fly.io provides the cloud infrastructure for safely running these AI agents.
The integration focuses on enhancing the safety and deployment of AI agents.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These new models allow for fast, low-latency, and cost-free execution of typed decisions.
Decision models can process text to provide probabilistic answers to yes/no questions, choices, or scores.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges the gap between proprietary AI services and local, open-weight models.

stories.title: Apple teases MacBook Pro event next week
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Apple is holding a product launch event on October 28th.
The event is expected to unveil new Macs, including a refreshed iPad Mini.
A key focus is anticipated to be a new MacBook Pro featuring an OLED display.

stories.title: Amazon is funding a new nuclear plant in Indiana
stories.author: Jess Weatherbed
bullet_points: Amazon is investing in a new nuclear energy facility in Indiana.
The project partners with X-energy and American Electric Power (AEP).
The plant aims to provide up to 960 MW of carbon-free energy, replacing a coal station.

stories.title: Russian spacecraft maneuvers in "extreme proximity" to satellite used by Ukraine
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: A Russian spacecraft (Kosmos 2612) performed a maneuver near a satellite used by Ukraine (ICEYE-X36).
The maneuver involved closing to 'extreme proximity' between the two objects.
The incident raises geopolitical and space safety concerns regarding orbital proximity operations.

stories.title: Accused OpenAI spy had folder called “Saudi Gov Docs,” FBI says
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: FBI investigation involves an ex-OpenAI engineer accused of spying.
Evidence found includes a folder labeled "Saudi Gov Docs."
US authorities fear Saudi government interference in the case.

stories.title: Batteries help reduce emissions, but how do we reduce their emissions?
stories.author: Scott K. Johnson
bullet_points: The article addresses the environmental impact of batteries, despite their role in reducing emissions.
A key proposed solution discussed is reducing the overall number of batteries required.
The topic highlights the growing need for sustainability within the battery technology sector.

stories.title: PSA: Patch your Plex media server before someone hacks it
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: A security researcher has identified a chain of four vulnerabilities affecting Plex media servers.
The news serves as a critical security advisory (PSA) urging users to patch their Plex installations immediately.
The attack vector involves chaining multiple vulnerabilities to compromise unpatched systems.

stories.title: AI game clones are making indie developers afraid to show their work
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: AI-generated game clones pose a threat to independent game developers.
The proliferation of AI clones is causing anxiety and hesitation among indie creators.
Delayed demos, such as the one mentioned, are cited as a symptom of this industry pressure.

stories.title: Rethinking the design space of Vanilla Pixel Diffusion Transformers
stories.author: Aniruddha Mahapatra
bullet_points: The research explores pixel-space diffusion models as an alternative to latent diffusion, aiming to bypass the lossy latent bottleneck.
The core innovation, MFlow, introduces an adaptive parameterization to improve the design space of vanilla diffusion transformers.
The work specifically investigates replacing standard velocity prediction ($\boldsymbol{u}$-prediction) with direct image prediction ($\boldsymbol{x_0}$-prediction) in diffusion transformers.

stories.title: AI-Driven Reproducibility and Analytical Robustness in Scientific Discovery
stories.author: Monica S. Lam
bullet_points: Proposes using LLM agents to automate the costly process of verifying research reproducibility and analytical robustness.
Introduces 'SEER-Repro,' a new benchmark utilizing the large-scale SEER cancer registry database for testing.
Focuses on a critical scientific bottleneck: ensuring the reliability and replicability of published research findings.

stories.title: Beyond SAEs: Consistent Concept Discovery with Sparse Coding
stories.author: Steffen Schneider
bullet_points: The paper addresses a key limitation of Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs): the variability of learned dictionaries across training runs.
It introduces Consistent Sparse Dictionary Learning (ConSDL) to improve the reliability and reproducibility of SAE-based analysis.
ConSDL achieves this by replacing the standard linear encoder with a per-sample sparse coding mechanism.

stories.title: DrugHarness: An Evolvable Agent Harness for Computational Drug Discovery
stories.author: Ming Hu
bullet_points: Introduces DrugHarness, an evolvable agent harness designed for computational drug discovery.
The system integrates over 80 scientific operations and biomedical resources, allowing agents to compose scientific workflows.
DrugHarness features conditional skill induction, enabling agents to adapt to changing evidence and constraints during the discovery process.

stories.title: Neural Expansion: A Unified Mechanism for How Deep Neural Networks Generalize
stories.author: Xiuwen Liu
bullet_points: Addresses the core mystery of how highly over-parameterized deep neural networks generalize effectively.
Introduces 'Neural Expansion,' a new unified geometric framework to explain generalization mechanisms.
Offers a mechanistic insight beyond existing theoretical paradigms like margin-based bounds or NTKs.

stories.title: GLOBE: Evolving Structured Agentic Memory for E-commerce Product Optimization in Generative Search
stories.author: Daeyeon Yi
bullet_points: Introduces GLOBE, a new framework for structured agentic memory designed to improve e-commerce product optimization.
Addresses a limitation where existing systems treat structured product listings as unstructured text, failing to retain successful optimization strategies.
Aims to enable language agents to continually self-improve by accumulating reusable strategies across various product categories for generative search.

stories.title: Beyond the Answer: Student-Conditioned Trace Construction for Reasoning Distillation
stories.author: Jian Li
bullet_points: Introduces ReDiST, a new framework for reasoning distillation in machine learning.
Addresses the limitation of answer-only supervision by focusing on constructing informative reasoning traces.
The framework conditions trace construction on the target student's learning needs and attempts.

stories.title: Quality-of-Transmission Estimation in Quantum Networks: Compute, Simulate, or Learn?
stories.author: Saddek Bensalem
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical need for timely and reliable Quality-of-Transmission (QoT) estimation in future quantum networks.
QoT estimation is vital for control-plane decisions like routing, scheduling, and entanglement provisioning.
The research explores the trade-offs between analytically computing, simulating, or learning the end-to-end entanglement fidelity.

stories.title: Learning without relearning physical symmetry: an SO(3)-equivariant convolutional network (CNN) on the sphere
stories.author: Lorne Whiteway
bullet_points: Introduces a novel SO(3)-equivariant convolutional network designed for data residing on the sphere.
Addresses a critical issue in physical sciences where lack of symmetry awareness leads to high simulation costs and biased results.
Presents a spherical implementation of a gauge equivariant mesh architecture for scientific analysis.

stories.title: CocoRNA: Collective RNA Design with Cooperative Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Ke Li
bullet_points: Introduces CocoRNA, a new framework for RNA inverse design using cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning.
Addresses the computational challenge of designing RNA sequences to reliably fold into specific secondary structures.
The framework simplifies the complex design task by decomposing it into smaller, collaboratively solved sub-problems.

stories.title: AI-Driven Reproducibility and Analytical Robustness in Scientific Discovery
stories.author: Monica S. Lam
bullet_points: Proposes 'SEER-Repro,' a benchmark to automate the evaluation of research reproducibility and analytical robustness.
Investigates the use of LLM agents to reduce the costly manual effort required for scientific validation.
Applies the methodology to a real-world, large-scale medical dataset (SEER database) concerning cancer research.

stories.title: Beyond the Answer: Student-Conditioned Trace Construction for Reasoning Distillation
stories.author: Jian Li
bullet_points: Introduces ReDiST, a framework for constructing reasoning traces that go beyond simple answer-only supervision.
The method conditions trace construction on the target student's characteristics to improve learning.
Aims to enhance knowledge transfer in evidence-rich reasoning by considering trace content and learner accessibility.

stories.title: Acceptance Is Not Speed: Length Inflation in Training-Free Lossy Speculative Decoding
stories.author: Hongyang Zhang
bullet_points: The paper investigates 'length inflation' when using lossy speculative decoding, challenging traditional speed metrics.
Lossless speculative decoding maintains the target model's output distribution, making its efficiency metrics reliable.
Relaxed (lossy) verification can accept tokens that alter the output distribution, leading to longer generated completions.

stories.title: Steering beyond Language: Improving Multilingual Training-Free Text Embeddings via Paired-Residual Subspace Removal
stories.author: Manabu Okumura
bullet_points: Presents the first systematic study on multilingual, training-free text embeddings derived from LLMs.
Identifies a language-conditioned embedding geometry where semantically equivalent sentences are misaligned across different languages.
Proposes a method, Paired-Residual Subspace Removal, to improve these multilingual embeddings.

stories.title: VocalGrad: Evaluating Acoustic Perception in Audio Language Models
stories.author: Hitomi Yanaka
bullet_points: Large Audio Language Models (LALMs) are moving beyond basic speech understanding to incorporate paralinguistic cues like emotion recognition.
A key challenge remains in how reliably these models utilize raw acoustic information when it is mixed with spoken language.
Current evaluation benchmarks are insufficient because they fail to separate genuine acoustic perception from complex, higher-level reasoning.

stories.title: Stress-Testing Gemini 4 Argon: Building a 3D Flutter Kart Game in 15 Prompts with Zero Assets
stories.author: leehack
bullet_points: The article explores using advanced AI models (Gemini 4 Argon) for complex, creative coding tasks.
It demonstrates the capability of frontier models to build a 3D Flutter game using only text prompts (15 prompts, zero assets).
The piece highlights a gap in current AI coding benchmarks, which often focus on simpler applications like CRUD dashboards.

stories.title: Your agent's retry bug isn't an AI problem. It's a distributed-systems problem with an LLM on top.
stories.author: cyclopt_dimitrisk
bullet_points: The article argues that common failures in AI agents (like retry bugs) are fundamentally distributed systems issues, not inherent LLM problems.
It critiques the typical 'happy path' demonstration of AI agents, which glosses over real-world failure modes.
The piece suggests that building robust agents requires addressing underlying infrastructure and system design challenges alongside LLM capabilities.

stories.title: I built an AWS agent that scores any GitHub repo before you clone it
stories.author: sarvar_04
bullet_points: A new tool, RepoPilot, uses AWS Lambda and Bedrock to score GitHub repositories.
The tool assesses repositories for potential risks, such as those posing as AI skills or malicious servers.
The concept addresses the growing threat of fake or compromised repositories in the development ecosystem.

stories.title: AI Made Coding Faster. Now Teams Are Cutting the Process That Catches Risky Changes
stories.author: pixel-wraith
bullet_points: AI tools are significantly accelerating the coding process.
Teams are reportedly streamlining or removing traditional quality gates to maintain development speed.
The underlying tension is balancing development velocity ('reduce friction') against risk mitigation.

stories.title: How Can Text Inside a Document Hijack an AI Agent?
stories.author: aditya_d_sharma
bullet_points: The article explores a security vulnerability where text within a document could potentially compromise an AI agent.
It focuses on the risk of AI agents being manipulated or 'hijacked' via input data, such as emails.
This highlights critical concerns regarding prompt injection and data security in AI applications.
